alternates.gemma4_ruleC_serve.json: Multi-probe category factor (rule C): fires on L21 last OR L20 last. Measured live at 626/675 CySec and 24/234 CatQA, against this kit's 558/23. NOT the default -- it was served, measured and rolled back. Kept here because it is reproducible, and it resolves the candidate bundle from this directory, same as the default operator.

gate.threshold_rule_meaning: The 12th-largest score on the 140 fit-reference prompts, so exactly 11 of them fire. R3 never sees an evaluation corpus, so this kit's CatQA leak is an out-of-sample measurement rather than a constraint that was fitted.

method.name: M1_subcat_Tridge_lam16
method.summary: Closed-form, no gradient training. Eigendecomposition of the subcategory-centred scatter (divisor 225 = 100 + 140 - 1 - 14), ridge-whitened mean difference with alpha = lambda[15]. 240 forward passes total.

corpus.not_redistributed: The 240 fit prompts are NOT in this kit; only the handful quoted in canaries.json are. The md5s above identify them so a re-fit can be shown to have used the same corpus.
corpus.overlap_with_evaluation_corpora: zero, checked by key against all 11 evaluation corpora

refusal_direction.recipe: difference-of-means then orthogonalize against the harmless centroid, at L21 'last'. r_unit = unit(raw - <raw,gd>gd) where raw = unit(mean(harmful) - mean(harmless)) and gd = unit(mean(harmless)), on RAW rows. Heretic's orthogonalize_direction, after Arditi et al. 2024.
refusal_direction.variant: 5-prompt 'blind' kit: 1 harmful + 4 harmless build the direction, while the calibration is measured on a separate 692-harmful + 554-harmless corpus. That split is why mu_hm_cos is +0.137 and not ~0: the direction is orthogonal to a 4-prompt centroid, but mu_hm_cos is measured against a different 554-row corpus.
refusal_direction.source_field_is_misleading: this file's own `source` names two blobs, 'gemma_dir90.pt (dir_gemma4-26B_sep.pt)'. Only the FIRST is the provenance: unit(gemma_dir90.pt['d']['21.attn_out']) is cosine 1.00000000000 to the shipped r_unit, max elementwise diff 2.6e-09. dir_gemma4-26B_sep.pt is a DIFFERENT direction at cosine 0.906, built by the full-corpus variant that the qwen36 kit ships. The field is left as-is because the served artifact is byte-pinned to the live evaluation.
refusal_direction.calibration_reproduced: every sidecar field to <=5.6e-16, z_harm_mean bit-identical, recomputed from gemma_pool681_acts.pt with harmless=554 and harmful=692 derivation rows (the 80 para_* and 100 adv_* rows held out), sd ddof=1, linear percentiles.
refusal_direction.direction_not_reproduced_bit_exactly: cosine 0.9735. The 5-prompt kit's own activation capture did not survive, so its rows were taken from pool681, whose render and padding differ; sep(21) comes out 2.7849 against the blob's 2.8285. The identity of the single harmful prompt is documented but not bit-verified.
refusal_direction.operating_point: at the policy floor s_ref_z >= 1.50 (cosine +0.214372): 28/554 harmless = 5.1%, 692/692 derivation harmful, 180/180 held-out para_*/adv_*.

bio.note: wmdp_cyber is a pass-rate TARGET (firing is correct); the two bio corpora are leakage non-targets (firing is a false positive). The two bio corpora disagree by two orders of magnitude on the same model and operator -- 4/637 vs 0/498 -- and across models WMDP-bio scores ~+0.05 higher than SOSBench-bio on both gemma4 and qwen36, which points at the multiple-choice framing rather than biology content. Not isolated by a manipulation.

known_gaps: The mid/late rescue supplies 3 of the 4 wmdp_bio fires, so what little bio leak there is comes from the rescue rather than the threshold.
The mid/late rescue supplies 82 of the 558 recorded fires. The rescue is not covered by the threshold rule, so that 14.7% of delivered recall rests on a separate mechanism.

THE CLIENT'S OWN CHAT RENDER IS ACCEPTED AS AN OBSERVATION PREFILL. This family does not override is_baseline_prefill, so it uses the base rule in families/base.py, whose first statement is `del u1_start` -- there is no u1_start guard, only `suffix_len <= 12`. Measured 2026-11-03 against google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it's own tokenizer (marker positive control passed: encode('<|turn>user\n') == (105, 2364, 107), encode('<turn|>') == 106, encode('<bos>') == 2): the observation render build_raw_prompt(mode='baseline', include_bos=True) is (u1_start=15, suffix_len=9), and apply_chat_template() is (u1_start=4, suffix_len=9) -- the SAME suffix length, with suffix ids reported identical. apply_chat_template(enable_thinking=True) is (11, 5), i.e. BELOW the observation, so tightening the ceiling cannot exclude it either. All three publish. Only u1_start separates them and it is discarded, so no rule over suffix_len alone -- bounded or exact-membership -- can fix this; porting qwen36's arm verbatim would not, since its `u1_start > 3` threshold is calibrated for Qwen's 45 and gemma4's client render sits at 4. CONSEQUENCE, from source (serving/middleware.py:350 probes, then :420 forwards the caller's untouched payload to /v1/chat/completions, which vLLM renders with the checkpoint template): the answer-generation prefill publishes after the probe and overwrites the decision the gate just made with one pooled under a different prefix -- the client render carries no system turn at all -- and with CYBERGATE_DUMP_ACTS_DIR set it appends a second unlabelled fp16 row per request. The routing of the request itself is unaffected: gate_info is computed from the probe's record before that dispatch. BOUND: the renders and the predicate outcomes are measured; the overwrite and the second dump row are derived from the call order in source and have NOT been confirmed live. The one-request dump row count is the control that would confirm them -- +1 is correct, +2 is this gap -- and it has not been run for this family. Also unmeasured: whether canaries.json's measured_score values were read from the probe's record or from the overwriting one. The fix belongs upstream of the predicate: the probe should identify itself rather than be inferred from its shape, since the middleware already dispatches it distinguishably (/v1/completions, max_tokens=1, add_special_tokens=False).

THE BOUNDED `suffix_len <= 12` RULE HAS NO LOWER BOUND, AND THE MARGIN IS ONE CONSTANT. Measured 2026-11-03: the shortest Pass-2 render reachable through the shipped routes is closed_loop_step1 / sandwich_step1 at 81 tokens, i.e. 69 tokens of margin above the ceiling. That 81 decomposes as 5 for the turn header, 3 for thought_open and 73 for OPEN_THINK_PREFIX, so the entire margin rests on the token length of one constant in cybergate/boilerplate.py; shorten it below roughly 5 tokens and the step1 renders begin publishing with nothing else changing. Separately, build_raw_prompt sets `rubric = FAKE_THINK_RUBRIC if custom_think_text is None else custom_think_text` (families/base.py:446), so passing an EMPTY STRING erases the 110-token rubric and collapses preclosed / preclosed_no_opener from 134 to 9 -- exactly the observation's suffix length, which publishes. Not reachable from the serving path, which never passes custom_think_text to those modes (think_routes.py:252 passes only post_think_opener), but reachable through the public build_raw_prompt_for_model(..., mode='preclosed', custom_think_text=''). An exact-membership rule would not have this failure mode.
